notes: Map quality vs rules: all internal links are U/D with ACL downstream and OHS/PL upstream; CF only to Stripe (justified by expert 'industry standard'); ACL to the messy video provider; no SK; no cycles. Fully rule-compliant. However, two cycle-breaking flips invert the natural direction stated in the ground-truth facts: facts say 'Scheduling needs to know whether a tutor may teach (from Trust & Safety)' and 'Pricing reads the rating', but the map has Scheduling upstream of TutorVetting (T&S calls 'close/open calendar') and Reviews/TutorCatalog pushing into Pricing's API. Both flips were accepted only through [improvised] replies (6.1, 6.2, 7), and the loops themselves were created by improvised facts (5.5 Complaints reads Scheduling's lesson record; 2.7 suspension cancels future lessons). The simulated expert's agreeableness on improvised questions is doing a lot of work here; a real expert might reject 'T&S calls Scheduling's calendar API'. The Pricing 'everyone feeds it' design is defensible (Finance's calculator as a published-language service), but registering rates/ratings duplicates data ownership. Lesson Delivery merge into Scheduling: sound against the facts. Ground truth names no delivery team (teams list: T&S, Scheduling, Billing, Payouts, Community, Complaints, Finance), the no-show rule is 'we decide ourselves', the webhook churn is a technical reason handled by the ACL, and Lesson Ended remains the hand-off pivot to Billing. The ownership-by-Scheduling answers were improvised but consistent with the facts. The critic's DISAGREE that triggered the merge was well reasoned. Improvisation: 26 '[improvised]' markers. Rounds 2, 3 and 6-7 are mostly improvised, so much of the finer structure (slots in Scheduling, payouts held on suspension, frozen price, calendar API) rests on invented facts. The core assertion-relevant boundaries (suspension owner, Pricing, Billing, Payouts) come from scripted facts. Cost: 258,810 tokens and 1081 s, about 3.8x the tokens and 6x the time of the baseline. It made 8 expert round trips (heavy for a busy expert) and about 20 critic verdicts. Mechanical checks all passed: validator ok, 8 canvases, report, final message 252 words. Eval critique: assertion 8 is satisfied trivially by any acyclic map. It does not check whether the flips used to reach acyclicity contradict ground-truth directions (e.g. T&S -> Scheduling eligibility). Consider adding an assertion that 'Scheduling learns tutor eligibility from Trust & Safety' or that flips are not justified solely by improvised answers.
